Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
226 AM MST Sun Mar 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Record breaking temperatures will continue through the end of 
  the weekend, likely extending into the upcoming workweek.

- Extreme Heat Warnings remain in effect for lower desert areas 
  through this evening.

- The unprecedented afternoon heat will be dangerous, especially
  with any strenuous or long-duration outdoor activities without
  proper hydration and taking breaks in the shade, or air
  conditioning. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Current objective analysis reveals zonal flow stretching across 
much of the western tier of the CONUS with the center of the the 
abnormally strong high pressure that has been entrenched over the 
Desert Southwest now a bit further south. This less amplified 
pattern appears to be a result of a potent low near the Gulf of 
Alaska that has been eroding away at H5 heights. The good news is,
this suppression of the ridge will result in relative cooldown 
for the region. The not so great news is that record high 
temperatures are likely to continue as H5 heights continue to run 
at or above the 99th percentile against climatology, indicating an
abnormally warm air mass for this time of year.

Temperatures this afternoon for desert locales will be around 3-5 
degrees lower compared to what has been observed over the past few 
days, but afternoon highs will remain close to 20 degrees above 
normal for early spring with max values right around 100 degrees. 
Model guidance indicates that the ridge will attempt to rebound, 
bringing back all-time record atmospheric heights by the front half 
of the upcoming workweek, but the thermal profile will take a bit 
longer to reflect this increase. Readings Monday and Tuesday will be 
some of the "coolest" we have seen since the middle of last week 
with middle and upper 90s being common. 
   
&&

.LONG TERM /WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
The longer term outlook does not offer much relief as the regional 
thermal profile catches up to the above-mentioned strengthening 
of the high, translating to a continuation of abnormally hot 
conditions for the latter portion of the month. H5 heights will 
rise to around 588-590dm, once again near climatological records, 
by Wednesday, ushering in the return of widespread triple digit 
heat for the lower deserts. This level of heat will continue to 
break daily records for many locations. In fact, Phoenix Sky 
Harbor has already set 4 consecutive daily records, and that is 
likely to extend to at least 11 by the end of the current forecast
window. The only noticeable weather change is projected during 
the upcoming week is a compact trough traversing the Great Basin 
by as early as Wednesday as it rides around the periphery of the 
center of the high. However, the only expected change would be 
some breezy to locally windy conditions for parts of our forecast 
area. Even with some lower heights associated with the 
disturbance, temperatures will not be impacted as the ridge 
remains the dominant feature. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0520Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
No major aviation weather concerns under increasing high cirrus
cloud decks can be expected throughout the TAF period. Winds will
continue to exhibit the typical diurnal tendencies with sustained
speeds aob 10 kts along some intermittent gusts in the teens 
Sunday afternoon/early evening.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major aviation weather concerns under passing high cirrus cloud
decks can be expected throughout the TAF period. At KIPL, winds
will generally be out of the west throughout the period while at
KBLH, winds will fluctuate between the south and southwest. Speeds
will generally remain aob 10 kts, although some intermittent
sundowner gusts near 20 kts will be possible once again at KIPL 
Sunday evening.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Record high temptress along with dry conditions will persist 
through the remainder of the weekend and into the upcoming week. 
MinRHs will generally range between 5-10%, with portions of the 
western districts being the exception during the front half of 
workweek. Increase in Gulf of California moisture will push RH 
values for these areas closer to 15-20% Monday and Tuesday. MaxRH 
values will follow a similar pattern with readings generally 
between 20-40% during much of the next seven days, as higher 
readings closer to 50-70% for some western districts locales. 
Winds will be generally light and follow diurnal trends through 
much of the foreast with typical afternoon upslope breeziness. 
More widespread and stronger gusts may come into play during the 
middle and latter portion of the week. With very dry air in place,
any stronger winds would result in periods of elevated fire 
weather conditions.
